A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Audio-Visual Instance Segmentation and AVISeg. All supplied text, figures, tables and equations support comparison. V1 has no appendix; v2 includes readable Supplementary Material, Sections 8–14. The substantial scientific revisions do not prevent comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original AVISeg experiments with ResNet-50 and Swin-Base in Table 1, plus predicted segmentation examples in Figure 6.

after.justification: V2 reports original comparative experiments, ablations and zero-shot evaluations in Tables 2–6, alongside qualitative comparisons and failure cases in the supplementary material.

M1.justification: V1's Mask2Former baseline uses TPAVI fusion and aggregated audio queries. V2 introduces AVISM's separate frame-level localizer and video-level token tracker, with frame/video audio-visual fusion, shifted-window temporal attention, video queries and query-similarity supervision. This substantially changes the architecture and tracking procedure.

E1.justification: V1 includes panoramic/360-degree videos and YT-ALL as a source; v2 removes that scenario and source while retaining music, speaking, machine and animal coverage. V2 also introduces evaluated COCO pretraining and OVIS fine-tuning configurations in Table 6. These change represented training data and input environments, beyond the increased annotation count.

E2.justification: V1 compares only its own model's two backbones. V2 Table 2 adds six VIS comparators, including Mask2Former-VIS, VITA and LBVQ, plus AVSegFormer and COMBO. Table 3 separately evaluates Sam4AVS, BuboGPT-7B, PG-Video-LLaVA-7B and AL-Ref-SAM 2 in zero-shot settings.

E3.justification: The labeled set grows from 117 to 926 videos; the 84/33 training/test split becomes 616/105/205 training/validation/test. Training changes from 6,000 iterations with batch size 12 to 48,000 with batch size 1, and the prediction threshold changes from 0.5 to 0.3. V2 adds HOTA, FSLA and their submetrics, replaces AP/AR breakdown reporting, and introduces controlled comparator and zero-shot protocols.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's backbone comparison and illustrative predictions, v2 tests frame/video fusion components, window size versus frame capacity, and backbone/pretraining choices in Tables 4–6. Supplementary Figures 7–10 add comparative case studies and failures involving multiple same-category sound sources.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Both present point estimates; additional result rows do not change this reporting practice.

E6.justification: V1 Table 1 reports AP values of 31.5 and 35.6 for ResNet-50 and Swin-Base. V2 Table 2 reports ResNet-50 AVISM at 42.78 FSLA, 61.73 HOTA and 40.57 mAP, alongside substantially expanded comparator, zero-shot, ablation and qualitative findings. Changed datasets, models and protocols prevent interpreting these as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The AVIS problem definition and trajectory-IoU formula are substantially retained. V2 introduces the novel FSLA definition, matching requirements, threshold averaging and silent/single/multiple-source submetrics, with Algorithm 1. This adds substantive formal evaluation content, although the pseudocode does not explicitly implement all class/count correctness checks stated in the prose.

C1.justification: The first-task/benchmark claim remains. V2 adds FSLA as a contribution, claims comparative superiority across reported metrics, and positions AVISeg as a benchmark exposing large multimodal models' instance-localization and temporal-understanding weaknesses. V1 presents only an initial baseline evaluated with two backbones.

C2.justification: V1 mainly interprets stronger-backbone benefits and successful predictions. V2 adds explanations of temporal fusion, window-size tradeoffs and OVIS pretraining effects, critiques mAP's suitability, and analyzes multimodal-model limitations. Sections 13–14 explicitly discuss same-category sound ambiguity and the limitations of offline processing for real-time applications.

D1.justification: V2 adds loss weights, query counts, window settings, frozen AudioSet-pretrained VGGish details, inference resizing, annotation-tool information and extensive comparator adaptations and prompts. Hardware changes from six to two Quadro 6000 GPUs. Some v1 disclosures, including weight decay, backbone learning-rate multiplier and two-frame training clips, are no longer stated.

R1.justification: V2 substantially revises the research positioning around VITA-style object-token association, newer AVS methods such as AVSegFormer and COMBO, and multimodal foundation-model evaluation. Its supplementary discussion adds substantial engagement with grounding pipelines, large models, streaming attention and audio disentanglement, extending v1's narrower VIS/AVS framing.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and much of the main narrative are rewritten. V2 separates task/metric definitions from the model, enumerates contributions, reorganizes experiments and moves implementation information into an extensive supplement. Binary segmentation terminology changes from AVSD to AVOS, and author/affiliation text is revised.

P2.justification: The task illustration becomes a temporal sequence, dataset graphics become a multi-panel statistical display, and the architecture is redrawn around frame/video processing with a separate fusion diagram. V2 adds comparison and ablation tables, multimodal pipeline diagrams, and extensive audio-aligned qualitative and failure panels. These exceed numerical updates or renumbering.

improvement.justification: V1 offers a small labeled subset and a two-backbone demonstration without competing-method comparisons. V2 adds a substantially developed benchmark, comparisons with shared backbones and training budgets, diagnostic ablations, implementation details and explicit failure analysis. These materially strengthen empirical support, including HOTA/mAP evidence independent of FSLA. Panorama coverage is lost, FSLA pseudocode incompletely specifies its correctness checks, and run-level uncertainty remains absent, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial evidential and reproducibility gains.
